items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true.
Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: target-kata,role=target
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
items.risk_note: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break workloads that write under /tmp, /var, /etc, or application paths.
items.manual_recommendation: Identify writable paths and move them to explicit volumes or emptyDir mounts first.
items.simulation_hint: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break workloads that write under /tmp, /var, /etc, or application paths.

items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.

items.manual_recommendation: Confirm whether the workload needs Kubernetes API access before disabling automount.
items.simulation_hint: Disabling token automount will break workloads that call the Kubernetes API from inside the pod.

items.title: Run workload as non-root
items.rationale: Root execution increases post-compromise impact and expands the effect of container escape or filesystem abuse.
actions: Set runAsNonRoot: true and a fixed non-zero runAsUser/runAsGroup.
Ensure the image filesystem permissions support the non-root UID.
Avoid sudo inside the image and remove unnecessary setuid binaries.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1

metadata:

spec:

    spec:

          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
items.risk_note: Changing to non-root can break startup if the image expects root-owned paths or privileged binds.
items.manual_recommendation: Validate file ownership, writable paths, and startup scripts before rollout.
items.simulation_hint: Changing to non-root can break startup if the image expects root-owned paths or privileged binds.

items.title: Drop Linux capabilities to the minimum required set
items.rationale: Capabilities such as CAP_NET_RAW or CAP_SYS_ADMIN increase kernel-facing attack surface and enable stronger in-cluster pivoting primitives.
actions: Drop ALL capabilities by default.
Re-add only narrowly required capabilities after validation.
Prefer application changes over retaining CAP_NET_RAW or CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
items.risk_note: Dropping all capabilities can break workloads that implicitly rely on raw sockets or privileged network operations.
items.manual_recommendation: Test with ALL dropped, then add back only the single capability proven to be required.
items.simulation_hint: Dropping all capabilities can break workloads that implicitly rely on raw sockets or privileged network operations.

items.title: Enable seccomp filtering
items.rationale: Seccomp reduces syscall surface and limits the effect of application-level compromise on the host kernel boundary.
actions: Set seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault at minimum.
Use Localhost profiles for stricter workloads if validated.
Test the runtime profile against the sandbox process tree before production rollout.

items.risk_note: RuntimeDefault seccomp can block uncommon syscalls used by desktop stacks, debuggers, or special runtimes.
items.manual_recommendation: Validate the workload under RuntimeDefault before enforcing in production.

items.title: Disallow privilege escalation
items.rationale: allowPrivilegeEscalation=false prevents gaining more privilege through setuid binaries or similar execution paths.
actions: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.
Remove setuid/setgid binaries not required by the workload.
Rebuild the image if privilege-granting tools are bundled by default.
